notes.statement: Verberne et al. (2022) identified a DNA methylation episignature of 150 CpG probes in peripheral blood from 8 patients with pathogenic or likely pathogenic JARID2 variants (6 deletions, 1 frameshift, 1 splice site) compared with 56 matched controls. Hierarchical clustering, MDS, and leave-one-out cross-validation showed robust, reproducible separation, and an SVM classifier showed full sensitivity and specificity versus controls and 57 other neurodevelopmental disorders.
quotes: Our three-step feature selection procedure yielded 150 probes (Tables S1 and S2) with which we observed a clear clustering of patients and controls, based on hierarchical clustering and MDS visualizations.

All the samples with (likely) pathogenic JARID2 variants received MVP scores near 1, while all the control samples and case samples from other neurodevelopmental disorders received low MVP scores. Therefore, we conclude that our model has full sensitivity and specificity.

notes.statement: Verberne et al. (2022) found that 3 patients carrying JARID2 missense variants of uncertain significance (R788Q in 2 unrelated patients and E644K) clustered with controls and received MVP scores near zero. Given nonspecific phenotypes and absence of characteristic facial features, the authors suggested these missense variants might very well be benign, although negative episignature results do not rule out pathogenicity.
quotes: The three patients with JARID2 VUSs were also supplied into the model and received MVP scores near zero, indicating the dissimilarity of their methylation profile to the identified JARID2-neurodevelopmental syndrome episignature (Figure 5).
As episignatures may only be used to upgrade a VUS to (likely) pathogenic if the related episignature is present, these negative results do not rule out pathogenicity.
we think that these JARID2 missense variants might very well be benign variants and that the phenotype of these patients is caused by another, currently unknown, genetic aberration.

notes.statement: Verberne et al. (2022) detected no significant differentially methylated regions with DMRcate, but among the 150 episignature probes found 7 small regions, 2 annotated to genes linked to abnormal neurologic development (NLGN2 and ADGRL2); gene set enrichment analysis did not yield consistent pathways, apart from enrichment for the endochondral ossification pathway.
quotes: Using the DMRcate algorithm with 5% mean methylation difference and a minimum of three CpGs, no significant DMRs were detected.
However, two of these seven regions were annotated to genes previously linked with aberrant neurological development.
However, we did detect enrichment of genes annotated to the endochondral ossification pathway (Webgestalt, Wikipathway).

notes.statement: Verberne et al. (2022) described JARID2-neurodevelopmental syndrome, caused by JARID2 haploinsufficiency, as characterized by developmental delay, cognitive impairment ranging from borderline intellectual functioning to severe intellectual disability, hypotonia, autistic features, and behavior abnormalities, with dysmorphic features including high anterior hairline, broad forehead, deeply set eyes, infraorbital dark circles, depressed nasal bridge, bulbous nasal tip, and full lips.
quotes: It is characterized by developmental delay, cognitive impairment (ranging from borderline intellectual functioning to severe intellectual disability), hypotonia, autistic features and behavior abnormalities.
Dysmorphic facial features include high anterior hairline, broad forehead, deeply set eyes, infraorbital dark circles, depressed nasal bridge, bulbous nasal tip and full lips.

notes.statement: Cadieux-Dion et al. (2022) reported JARID2 variants that were inherited from mildly affected parents, which showed that the disorder has variable expressivity.
quotes: In addition, we report inheritance of JARID2 variants from mildly affected parents, demonstrating the variable expressivity of the disease.

notes.statement: Cadieux-Dion et al. (2022) noted that intragenic JARID2 copy number variants were highly prevalent in their series, and they emphasized the importance of exon-level analysis.
quotes: We also note the high prevalence of intragenic JARID2 copy number variants, emphasizing the importance of exon-level analysis.

notes.statement: Cadieux-Dion et al. (2022) identified palatal abnormalities and heart defects as part of the phenotype of JARID2-related intellectual disability.
quotes: confirming this gene-disease association and highlighting palatal abnormalities and heart defects as part of the phenotype

notes.statement: Verberne et al. (2021) used chromosome microarray, exome sequencing, and GeneMatcher to identify individuals with deletions or SNVs involving JARID2; several variants were predicted to cause haploinsufficiency through nonsense-mediated mRNA decay, and the authors concluded that JARID2 haploinsufficiency leads to a clinically distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome.
quotes: Several of these variants are likely to result in haploinsufficiency due to nonsense-mediated messenger RNA (mRNA) decay.
We report that JARID2 haploinsufficiency leads to a clinically distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome, thus establishing gene-disease validity for the purpose of diagnostic reporting.

notes.statement: Verberne et al. (2021) noted that JARID2, located on chromosome 6p22.3, regulates histone methyltransferase complexes and is expressed in human neurons.
quotes: JARID2, located on chromosome 6p22.3, is a regulator of histone methyltransferase complexes that is expressed in human neurons.

notes.statement: Zahir et al. (2016) had earlier found a CNV involving only exon 6 of the JARID2 gene, apparently de novo, in 7 patients with intellectual disability. Exon 6 encodes one of a series of repeated motifs. When they studied this variant in two cohorts with a genotype-phenotype assessment, they concluded that the exon 6 CNV was benign, with a population frequency above 14%, although it could still have a contributory effect.
quotes: Previously, we found a CNV involving only exon 6 of the JARID2 gene occurred apparently de novo in seven patients.
We find the JARID2 exon 6 CNV is benign, with a high population frequency (>14%), but nevertheless could have a contributory effect.

notes.statement: Barøy et al. (2013) proposed that JARID2 haploinsufficiency causes a recognizable neurodevelopmental syndrome. Its features were cognitive impairment ranging from borderline IQ to severe intellectual disability, gait disturbance and a distinctive face with prominent supraorbital ridges, deep-set eyes, dark infraorbital circles and midface hypoplasia.
quotes: Patients carrying JARID2 deletion manifested with cognitive impairment, gait disturbance and a characteristic facial appearance
Due to the characteristic facial appearance, JARID2 haploinsufficiency might represent a clinically recognizable neurodevelopmental syndrome.

notes.statement: Barøy et al. (2013) studied about 3,600 patients with neurodevelopmental disorders by aCGH. Four patients had de novo 6p22.3 deletions that shared a 189-kb smallest region of overlap (SRO I) containing JARID2 and DTNBP1. The authors judged DTNBP1 unlikely to explain the phenotype and considered JARID2 the critical gene.
quotes: The smallest region of overlap (SRO I) in Patients 1-4 (189 kb) included the genes JARID2 and DTNBP1
Thus a link between DTNBP1 haploinsufficiency and the features seen in our patients is unlikely.
we suggest that JARID2 is likely to be the critical gene within SRO I, and the main gene causing the neurodevelopmental syndrome in Patients 1–4.

notes.statement: In the 4 patients with JARID2 deletions, Barøy et al. (2013) found that JARID2 expression in leukocytes was significantly lower than in 8 controls (p ≤ 0.01).
quotes: JARID2 expression was significantly reduced in our patients compared to controls (p ≤ 0.01) (Figure 4A).

notes.statement: Barøy et al. (2013) reported that the same facial pattern was confirmed on photographs of 7 of 10 previously published patients with JARID2-containing deletions. Impaired balance or coordination and/or gait disturbance had been noted in 4 of those 10 patients.
quotes: when we carefully inspected the photos available for seven of these individuals, a similar facial pattern could be confirmed.
Impaired balance and coordination and/or gait disturbance were noted in four out of the 10 previously reported patients with JARID2 deletion (Patients 6, A, C and J, Table 2)

notes.statement: Barøy et al. (2013) found that the 3 patients whose deletions removed both JARID2 and ATXN1 had lower cognitive function than the patients missing only one of the genes. They suggested that losing both genes made the intellectual disability more severe.
quotes: Patients 1-3 presented with lower cognitive function than Patients 4 and 5, possibly due to the concomitant haploinsufficiency of both ATXN1 and JARID2.

notes.statement: Barøy et al. (2013) recommended sequencing JARID2 in patients with a similar phenotype when no deletion is found.
quotes: we suggest that this gene should be sequenced in future patients with a similar phenotype when a gene deletion is not present.
